title: 1986 AHSME Problem 4
statement:
Let \(S\) be the statement

“If the sum of the digits of the whole number \(n\) is divisible by \(6,\) then \(n\) is divisible by \(6.\)”

A value of \(n\) which shows \(S\) to be false is

solutions.text:
The digit sum of \(33\) is \(6,\) which is divisible by \(6.\) However, \(33\) is odd, so it is not divisible by \(6.\) Thus \(33\) makes the implication false.

Therefore the correct answer is B.
hints: A counterexample must satisfy the hypothesis but not the conclusion
Divisibility by \(6\) requires both divisibility by \(2\) and by \(3\)
